question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births in Japan in July 2026, as first reported in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (which also count foreign nationals in Japan).

target.what: Number of live births in Japan during July 2026, as counted in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (including foreign nationals resident in Japan)
target.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), Japan
target.cadence: monthly preliminary release, typically published roughly 2 months after the reference month (so the July 2026 preliminary figure would normally appear around September 2026, after the cutoff)
target.caveats: The July 2026 preliminary figure is not published as of the 2026-08-25 cutoff, so the target must be estimated. candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 births will be close to July births in recent years, adjusted for the ongoing downward trend and any calendar effects (number of weekdays, Obon timing). methods.rationale: July 2024 total births (p64) scaled by the Jan-May 2026 vs Jan-May 2025 cumulative ratio (p98/p99). Uses the same MHLW definition (total incl. foreign nationals) and the most recent cumulative yoy signal. Shared dependency: both target and signal come from MHLW preliminary statistics, so a definitional shift would move both. Failure mode: the Jan-May yoy may not represent July's yoy if the conception cohort shifted.

p64.role: July 2024 total live births in Japan (MHLW preliminary, incl. foreign nationals)

a2.role: year-on-year change factor from July 2025 to July 2026

methods.rationale: Anchors on July 2024 (p64) and applies a change factor for the two-year gap to July 2026, centered on flat yoy given the +0.4% Jan-May 2026 cumulative (p100) and -1.7% May 2026 (p97). The factor a2 is a dimensionless change factor, not a level. Failure mode: if the 2025-2026 decline accelerates, the estimate is too high; if births rebound, too low.

p94.role: May 2026 total live births in Japan (MHLW preliminary, incl. foreign nationals)

a1.role: July-to-June seasonal ratio of monthly births

methods.rationale: Uses the most recent observed month (May 2026, p94) and a July/June seasonal ratio (a1) to project July 2026. This route is weaker because it bridges two months (May to July) via a June-July ratio; it implicitly assumes May-June-July follow the 2024 seasonal shape. Failure mode: a June 2026 anomaly would not be captured.

p64.role: July 2024 total live births in Japan (MHLW preliminary, incl. foreign nationals)

methods.rationale: July 2024 level scaled by the observed Jan-May 2026/2025 cumulative ratio (p98/p99 = 1.0044). Same definitional series throughout. This is a deterministic version of m1 and shares its inputs, so it is not independent confirmation; it is included to let the code's uncertainty treatment reflect the ratio's sampling error. Failure mode: the Jan-May yoy may not carry into July.

assumptions.name: July-to-June seasonal ratio
assumptions.rationale: From MHLW 2024 monthly data, July (p64=62,306) / June (p65=55,313) ≈ 1.126. July consistently exceeds June in Japan because of the September-October conception peak and fewer holiday disruptions; the range reflects year-to-year variation in weekday composition and Obon timing.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a June 2026 total birth count to project July 2026; assumes the June-July seasonal pattern is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the 2026 June-July ratio deviates sharply from the 2024 pattern (e.g., a June 2026 preliminary count implying a ratio outside 1.05-1.20).

assumptions.name: July 2026 to July 2025 year-on-year change factor
assumptions.rationale: Jan-May 2026 cumulative births were +0.4% yoy (p100) and May 2026 was -1.7% yoy (p97), so the recent trend is roughly flat with slight downside. July 2026 is expected near July 2025, with a range reflecting monthly noise and the ongoing mild downward drift.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to July 2025 total births to project July 2026; assumes the recent flat yoy trend continues.
assumptions.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary count showing a sharp yoy break (e.g., >5% decline or >3% rise).

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: July 2024 births (p64) scaled by the Jan-May 2026/2025 cumulative ratio (p98/p99). Uses the only kept July target-history value and the most recent cumulative signal; assumes the July yoy change matches the Jan-May yoy change. Shared dependency: both p98 and p99 come from the same MHLW preliminary table.

methods.label: m2

p64.role: July 2024 total live births in Japan (MHLW preliminary, incl. foreign nationals)

a2.role: year-on-year change factor from July 2025 to July 2026

methods.rationale: July 2024 level times an explicit July 2025-to-2026 yoy factor. The factor is centered near flat because Jan-May 2026 is +0.4% but May 2026 is -1.7%; the range spans the recent trend. Failure mode: if the July 2026 yoy change reverts to the 2025 annual -2.2% decline, the estimate is too high.

methods.label: m4

p64.role: July 2024 total live births in Japan (MHLW preliminary, incl. foreign nationals)

methods.rationale: July 2024 births times the Jan-May 2026/2025 cumulative ratio. This is the same route as m1 but expressed as a formula; it shares p64, p98 and p99 with m1, so it is not independent confirmation. Failure mode: the July yoy change differs from the Jan-May yoy change.

kept.name: July-to-June seasonal ratio of monthly births
kept.rationale: From p64/p65 (July 2024 62,306 / June 2024 55,313 = 1.126); July is consistently the seasonal peak in the 2024 monthly table. Range reflects year-to-year variation in the July/June ratio and the fact that the anchor month is May 2026, not June 2026.
kept.applies_when: The July/June seasonal pattern of 2024 carries over to 2026 and May-to-July is a reasonable stand-in for June-to-July.
kept.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary figure showing the July/June ratio far outside 1.05-1.20, or evidence of a large shift in the seasonal birth pattern.

kept.name: July 2026 to July 2025 year-on-year change factor
kept.rationale: Jan-May 2026 cumulative births are +0.4% yoy (p98/p99) but May 2026 alone is -1.7% (p94/p95); the recent month is weaker than the year-to-date, so the July yoy factor is centered near flat with a range spanning roughly -6% to +6%.
kept.applies_when: The July 2026 yoy change is similar to the recent Jan-May 2026 trend rather than reverting to the 2025 annual decline.
kept.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary figure showing a yoy change well outside -6% to +6%.

kept.name: July 2026 to July 2024 two-year change factor
kept.rationale: Bridges the two-year gap from July 2024 (p64) to July 2026. 2025 annual births incl. foreigners fell 2.1% (p56/p318) and Jan-May 2026 is +0.4% (p98/p99), so the cumulative two-year change is roughly -1.7%; centered at 0.97 with a range spanning -10% to +4% to allow for July-specific deviation.
kept.applies_when: The July 2026 level is close to July 2024 adjusted by the cumulative national trend over 2025-2026.
kept.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary figure implying a two-year change well outside 0.90-1.04.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
